title: AI Caption Generation Flowchart
purpose: AI-powered caption generation from image upload through base64 encoding, OpenRouter API call, caption return, and later save as content.description
description: Frontend sends image file (multipart) to POST /api/v1/ai/caption. Multer middleware stores image in memory buffer. AI controller calls ai.service.ts generateCaption(imageBuffer, context?). Service base64-encodes the buffer and sends to OpenRouter/OpenAI via SDK with model gemma-3-27b-it:free. System prompt: 'Generate a short engaging caption for this image'. Response is caption text returned synchronously to frontend. Caption appears in DraftCard textarea; creator can edit, accept, or regenerate. Caption is later saved as content.description when content is created via POST /api/v1/content.

errorPaths.recovery: 30s delay in DraftCard AI handler, but no server-side retry
No retry — user must click AI caption again
File must be re-uploaded at smaller size

errorPaths.destination: Frontend loading spinner stalls until timeout

validationRules.rule: Only image files accepted (uploadAICaptionImage Multer config)
File stored in memory buffer before base64 encode
System prompt: 'Generate a short engaging caption for this image'

businessRules.rule: Image-to-caption is the only AI feature implemented
No content moderation pre-check before sending image to third-party API
No audit trail of what was sent to or received from the AI API
No retry or idempotency for failed API calls

securityConsiderations: CRITICAL: No NSFW pre-check — any image (including explicit/personal content) is sent to OpenRouter/OpenAI without content moderation pre-scan
User media transmitted to third-party API (OpenRouter/OpenAI) without explicit consent notice to user
No audit trail — no record of what images were sent, what captions were generated, or when
Base64 encoding loads entire image into memory again — doubles memory usage from Multer buffer
Synchronous blocking — frontend shows loading spinner until API responds; no streaming or background processing
performanceConsiderations: Synchronous HTTP call to OpenRouter — frontend blocks until response (typical 2–5s)
Base64 encoding increases size by ~33% over binary — larger request payload
5-second delay between consecutive requests (client-enforced) — 10 files = 50s minimum
No caching — identical images will re-trigger API calls and cost

annotations.text: No NSFW pre-check — images sent to third-party OpenRouter/OpenAI API without any content moderation pre-scan
No audit trail — no record of what was sent to AI or what was generated
Synchronous blocking — frontend shows loading spinner until API responds; no streaming or background processing
No retry/idempotency — 429 or 5xx errors propagate directly to user
